# dsh-tab-indicator
**English** | 简体中文

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) web
plugin that puts the agent's running/done state on the browser tab, so

you can
see from any other tab whether work is still running.
## Features

- **Live running badge** — while one or more root sessions run, the favicon
shows a blue badge with

the count (`1`, `2`, … `9+`).
- **Count instead of a dot** — a single run leaves the title untouched

; `(N)`
appears only when more than one run is active. There is no title dot.
- **Done check** — whe

n a run finishes, the tab shows a green check for about a
second. If other runs remain, the count ba

dge comes back; if none remain, the
check stays only while the tab is hidden or the window is unfocu

sed and clears
when you return.
- **Static by design** — the favicon is repainted only when the coun

t or the
running/done state changes. This avoids Chrome restarting its own favicon
loading indicator

on every frame, which makes the bookmark icon churn.
- **Theme aware** — uses the light or dark fav

icon variant the browser is
currently showing, regenerates it when the color scheme changes, and res

tores
the original `<link>` elements when idle.
- **No polling** — the host pushes a full snapshot o

ver Server-Sent Events; the
page catches up automatically after a host restart.
- **Local only** — n
o outbound requests and no DeepSeek API key.
## Requirements

- **DSH 0.2.1.x** with the web profile. Tested with `0.2.1-rc.3`.
- For development and tests, Node.

js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the DSH
requirement).
- No DeepSeek API key: the plugin never calls an ex

>=24.0.0` (the DSH
requirement).
- No DeepSeek API key: the plugin never calls an external service.

## Usage

- While one or more root sessions run, the favicon shows a blue count badge
(`1`, `2`, … `9+`). The

tab title is unchanged for one run and gets `(N)` when
more than one run is active.
- When a run fin

ishes, the tab shows a green check for about a second. If other
runs are still active, the count bad

ge returns. If nothing remains, the check
stays only while the tab is hidden or the window is unfocu

sed; it clears when
you return.
- The count is global to the DSH host, not limited to the current wo

rkspace; a
run in another session still counts.
- Subagent turns are part of their root turn and do

not add to the count.
- The count is **turn-level**. A background job that outlives its turn is not

counted; see Limitations.
- No polling: the host pushes a complete snapshot over SSE, and the browse

## Why the favicon is static

The icon is repainted only when the running count or the running/done state
changes. It is intention
ally not animated between those changes.

Chrome treats every `<link rel="icon">` href change as a fresh favicon load. Its
own loading indicat

or — including the one on the bookmark bar — restarts for
each load, so a continuously animated favi

con makes the bookmark icon churn.
Chrome has no native animated favicon (GIF favicons show the firs

t frame only,
and SVG/CSS animation is ignored), so there is no way to animate the icon
without that
reload behavior. A static badge is the deliberate trade-off.
## How it works

The plugin is a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch = ./cordis.patch.yml`, and tha

t patch inserts the
`dsh-tab-indicator` entry into the web profile. It has two halves:
| Half | File | Role |
| Host | `lib/index.js` | Tracks running root agents, publishes the SSE snapshot, serves `GET /dsh-t
ab-indicator/events` and `GET /dsh-tab-indicator/client.js`, and injects the client into the index p

age. |
| Browser | `client.js` | Injected into the DSH index page. Consumes SSE, decorates the title
, and paints the static count/check badge over the page's favicon. |
The SSE snapshot is small:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `ctx.agents.roots()` seeds the snapshot for agents that are already running
when the plugin loads.

- `agent/status` (`idle` / `running`) and `agent/disposed` keep it current.
- A 2-second reconcilia

tion against `ctx.agents.roots()` repairs a transition
missed across a plugin reload and removes a s

ession whose agent is no longer
running.
- `connection.requestRejection` guards the stream with the

same browser cookie
used by the rest of the Web API.
- `ctx.webServer.tapIndex` inserts
`<script def
er src="/dsh-tab-indicator/client.js?v=1">`.

The browser half (`client.js`) consumes the stream, decorates the title, and
paints a count/check ba

dge on a 64×64 canvas over the page's original favicon.
It repaints only when the count or state cha

n a 64×64 canvas over the page's original favicon.
It repaints only when the count or state changes.
## Privacy

- **No outbound requests** — the host makes no network calls, and the plugin
needs no DeepSeek API k

ey.
- **Local only** — the browser only talks to your local DSH server: the SSE
stream, the injected

client script, and the page's own favicon asset used to
draw the badge.
- **No telemetry** and no c

the page's own favicon asset used to
draw the badge.
- **No telemetry** and no credential handling.
## Limitations

- It tracks **turn-level** activity. A background job that outlives its turn is
not counted; adding

the jobs service would be the next step if that matters.
- It is a Web-profile plugin: it needs `web

Server` and `agents`.
- The favicon is a `data:image/png` URL. If a deployment adds a Content Securi

ty
Policy, `img-src` must allow `data:` (the current Web index has no CSP).
- A fully closed browser

cannot show anything, by definition.
- The favicon is static between state changes; see
Why the fav

Why the favicon is static.
